newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases marginally vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases marginally vs dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling eased marginally against the dollar in a moderately active market, commercial bank dealers said on Thursday.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a commercial mean of 59.11 against the dollar from 58.98 on Wednesday while against the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean of 99.15 from 98.77.
"The market (interbank) is very quiet. We're receiving a lot of enquiries but I think most people are hoping to buy at lower levels," a dealer said.
They said the shilling was trading at 58.70/59.40 levels.

The 60-level remained a technical and psychological barrier, some dealers said. They said that whereas exporters were happy to take advantage of the current levels, importers were holding off the market which they considered too expensive.
"They keep asking if CBK (Central Bank of Kenya) is going to come in," a dealer said.
Market analysts said market nerves seemed to have calmed, adding that the shilling was holding steady at the current levels -- resisting any pressure to weaken further.
The money market continued liquid with overnight rates at 8-12 percent compared to 12-14 percent on Friday.
